thesis: Wise rose about 2.7% to $11.225 (from $10.93) on 7.8x volume, gapping up the day after its Nov 12 H1 fiscal 2027 results (half year to Sept 30): net revenue rose 23% to about $1.45B; income before tax rose 9% to $334.9M; net income rose 6% to $249.2M; diluted EPS rose 8% with help from buybacks; and the company said it has nearly completed half of a buyback of more than $500M. It now expects full-year net revenue growth in the upper half of its 15-20% medium-term range and a pre-tax margin around the top of its 20-25% range. Counter-cases remain open: the pre-tax margin fell to about 23% from about 26% as operating expenses rose 28% on technology investment and US-listing compliance costs, and the legal picture is unsettled. A 2026 securities class action complaint names Wise, CEO Kristo Kaarmann and CFO Emmanuel Thomassin (filing date, court and allegations not confirmed by this run). Atlantic Money filed a competition complaint in February 2026. A report of a Belgian money-laundering probe is unverified, and Wise is seeking an HMRC settlement over customer tax errors. No scheduled ruling was found. The CEO's 2024 FCA fine over his personal tax disclosure is not a company restatement or plea. A confirmed revenue beat and raised growth outlook with margin compression and open legal matters unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Net revenue growth falls below the guided upper half of 15-20%, the pre-tax margin drops below 20%, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$10.93).
sources: London Stock Exchange (FCA concludes CEO investigation, 2024): https://www.londonstockexchange.com/news-article/WISE/fca-concludes-investigation-into-kristo-kaarmann/16734155

thesis: Keurig Dr Pepper rose about 2.6% to $36.34 (from $35.42) on 3.2x volume, the session after it priced an underwritten offering of 57,971,015 shares at $34.50 (a 2.6% discount), expected to close Nov 16. The roughly $2B of proceeds will repay or repurchase about $2B of debt ahead of the planned split into Beverage Co. and Global Coffee Co., targeted for early 2027. Shares fell about 5% on Nov 12 when the raise was announced, so today's volume and rebound reflect the offering's trading rather than new operating information; Jefferies reiterated a Hold. The share offering meets the dilution_risk criterion. Litigation: a long-running single-serve coffee antitrust case was allowed to proceed to trial (October 2026 report; no trial date found), plus consumer labeling class actions; no restatement found. An offering-driven, mechanical move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The offering settles, the split proceeds on schedule, and a company-disclosed operating result drives the shares.

thesis: DoubleVerify was flat at $13.555 (from $13.57) on 3.2x volume, about 0.3% below the $13.60-per-share cash price Nielsen agreed to pay (August 2026, about $2.15B enterprise value; 8-K). Shareholders approved the sale on Oct 29, closing is expected by Q1 2027 subject to regulatory approvals, and the company has suspended earnings calls while the deal is pending. The volume-spike and near-52-week-high signals reflect merger-arbitrage trading at the deal price, not new company information. Litigation: a securities class action (S.D.N.Y., No. 25-cv-04332, filed May 2025) and a December 2025 derivative suit remain pending with no scheduled ruling found; no restatement found. Upside is capped at $13.60, so the move is mechanical; low, avoid.
invalidation: The merger is terminated or its terms change, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.
sources: PPC Land (earnings calls halted until close): https://ppc.land/doubleverify-halts-earnings-calls-until-its-13-60-nielsen-sale-closes/

thesis: Cerebras rose about 11.1% to $108.59 (from $97.75) on 3.3x volume after its Nov 12 Q3 report: core revenue was $230.9M, the full-year revenue outlook was raised, Q4 core revenue guidance is $310-330M, management confirmed a Microsoft cloud agreement on the call, and coverage cites a forecast that revenue triples in 2027. Counter-cases remain open and are substantial: the Q3 loss of $0.67 per share was wider than estimated; the main IPO lock-up expired Nov 9-10, making up to about 171.1M shares eligible for sale; the CEO and CTO have sold more than $240M of shares under trading plans; Culper Research published a short report on Oct 28; and the stock had fallen about 46% over 60 days and remains about 41% below the $185 May IPO price. Litigation: a putative copyright class action over training data (N.D. Cal., filed October 2025), which the company is defending, with no scheduled ruling found; no securities suit or restatement found. Insider sales and lock-up expiry are not a share offering by the company, so no risk flag applies. A confirmed raise-and-new-customer catalyst with supply and loss counter-cases unresolved makes this medium.
invalidation: Q4 core revenue misses the $310-330M guide, the Microsoft agreement does not convert into disclosed revenue, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$97.75).

thesis: CG Oncology rose about 6.0% to $74.38 (from $70.15) on 2.9x volume, and this run found no company announcement or other cause dated today. The most recent company-specific items found are older: the rolling BLA for cretostimogene in high-risk BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, with the complete submission (final CMC module) expected in Q4 2026 and no FDA acceptance or PDUFA date found, and Phase 3 data in July 2026 after which an analyst kept a Buy rating. The litigation check found only Kuehn Law's August 2026 fiduciary-duty investigation of officers and directors (a solicitation, with no filed suit found) and no restatement. A move with no identified company catalyst ahead of a still-pending BLA submission makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The complete BLA is submitted and accepted with a PDUFA date, giving a company-disclosed catalyst.

thesis: TXNM Energy was flat at $58.83, about 1.2% below its 52-week high, trading as a pending Blackstone Infrastructure takeover (about $11.5B). Shareholders approved the deal in August 2025, and FERC, the Texas PUC, the FCC and the HSR waiting period have cleared it; NRC and New Mexico PRC approvals remain outstanding. In July 2026 the New Mexico PRC voted 2-1 to void a related $400M stock sale between TXNM/PNM and Blackstone, fined each company $100,000, and required an unwinding report, which coverage says will likely push back the merger timeline; a merits-hearing schedule was still to be set. The near-52-week-high signal reflects deal-bound trading, not new company information, and the main open item is a regulatory decision with no date found. A mechanical, deal-bound move makes this low; avoid.
invalidation: The New Mexico PRC rejects the merger or the deal is terminated, so the stock trades on fundamentals again.

thesis: Heartflow fell about 19.2% to $48.41 (from $59.92) on 2.1x volume after its Nov 12 Q3 report (8-K). Revenue grew 57% to $72.9M and beat estimates, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to $262-264M from $246-250M. But coverage says the raised guide leaves little room for growth in the remaining months of 2026, and investors took profits after the stock ran up near its 52-week high (up about 21% over 60 days through Nov 12); the CEO also sold about $2.17M of shares. The company still posts operating losses. It previously disclosed DOJ Civil Division civil investigative demands (October 2025) under the Anti-Kickback Statute and False Claims Act, with no scheduled step found, and it is the plaintiff in a patent suit against Cleerly (E.D. Tex.). No restatement or share offering was found. A strong quarter offset by an implied fourth-quarter slowdown leaves the evidence mixed; low, avoid.
invalidation: Q4 revenue beats the implied guide and 2027 guidance shows growth re-accelerating.
sources: Investing.com (earnings call, shares slip after hours): https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-heartflow-beats-q3-2026-eps-forecast-shares-slip-after-hours-93CH-5023580
Strawman (filing excerpt on DOJ civil investigative demands): https://strawman.com/reports/AYA/NewbieHK

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV slipped about 1.1% to $39.54 (from $39.99), still well above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today. Items found: the latest quarterly update (quarter ended Sept 30, 2026) reports $4.2B of cash and that IMVT-1402 succeeded in Immunovant's late-line rheumatoid arthritis study; an Investor Day is set for Dec 9; and STAT reported on Oct 21 that two Phase 3 noninfectious uveitis trials spanning 371 patients produced results that could open a large new market. The thesis rests on the company's Nov 9 fiscal Q2 release cited in the prior thesis: LISRAYA (brepocitinib) generated $31.0M of net product revenue in its first five weeks after approval. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the Phase 3 uveitis data are not an approval, and the sNDA is not expected until 1H calendar 2027. This stays medium.
invalidation: LISRAYA uptake stalls, or FDA feedback or full data reveal a uveitis safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). Centene rose about 1.4% to $71.26 (from $70.27), above the ~$68.03 pre-report level, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today; the items found were a Nov 6 price snapshot and a StockAnalysis summary of 21 analysts with a $74.50 average target. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58, a consolidated HBR of 92.7%, and 2026 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $5.20. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: roughly $0.50 of non-recurring 2026 EPS, Medicaid membership declines and margin pressure, the 2027 Arkansas Medicaid expansion exit, the 'Ohana Health Plan exit from Hawaii's Medicaid program on Dec 31, the $448M star-ratings dispute with HHS and CMS, and the Lunstrum v. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).
sources: EarningsWhispers (Q3 2026 results and guidance, prior thesis source): https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/CNC/202609

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal; trimmed toward its low-conviction target on Nov 9). NWL edged up about 0.3% to $5.78, just below the $5.82 cost, and this run's search found no November 2026 company news (only older price snapshots). It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance; the December 2025 productivity plan's restructuring charges run through 2026. No new negative fact has emerged, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
sources: Investing.com (NWL quote page, no Nov 13 items found): https://uk.investing.com/equities/newell-rubber

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 9 on the Nov 6 proposal). JFrog rose about 2.7% to $113.64 (from $110.60), touching a new 52-week high of $114.44, and this run's search found no company disclosure dated today (the items found were mid-2026 52-week-high reports). The thesis rests on the Nov 5 Q3 report (8-K): revenue grew 31% to $179.2M, cloud revenue grew 60%, net dollar retention rose to 124%, and free cash flow was $66.5M. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: GAAP operating income is still slightly negative, share-based compensation was $41.8M in the quarter, the Q4 revenue guide implies only about 2-3% sequential growth, and the size of any full-year raise against prior guidance remains unconfirmed. The early-exit guard applies (opened 4 trading days ago). This stays medium.
invalidation: Cloud growth or net dollar retention decelerates materially, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$74.62).
sources: Webull (Aug 2026 52-week-high report, no Nov 13 items found): https://www.webull.ca/news-detail/15475938813625344

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 12 on the Nov 11 proposal). SK Telecom's ADR rose about 1.2% to $34.54 (from $34.12), above the $33.91 fill and its 200-day average, and this run's search found no company news dated today; coverage found notes the ADR can also move with the Korean won and U.S. tariff sentiment. The thesis rests on the Nov 4 Q3 report: revenue of KRW 4.4973T, operating income of KRW 552.3B, net income of KRW 411.8B, and a KRW 830 quarterly dividend. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open: the year-over-year jump is measured against the hacking-hit Q3 2025, handset subscribers declined, and breach-related exposure (the suit to revoke the KRW 134.8B privacy fine and consumer-agency compensation orders) has no scheduled ruling found. The early-exit guard applies (opened 1 trading day ago). This stays medium.
invalidation: Operating income falls back below KRW 500B, a breach ruling or compensation order materially raises costs, or a close back below the pre-move level (~$33.11).
sources: SK Telecom newsroom (Q3 2026 results, prior thesis source): https://news.sktelecom.com/en/3336
